name: Fulfillment

planning_reference.reason: The approved Orders contract and greenfield product requirements are sufficient; no legacy code, runtime, data, infrastructure, IDs, migrations, or behavior is required.

expected_models.name: Fulfillment
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped execution batch for delivery or pickup, linked to one confirmed Order and protected by an explicit lifecycle and version.

expected_models.name: FulfillmentItem
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped allocation of a positive quantity from one confirmed OrderItem into one fulfillment batch.

expected_models.name: FulfillmentStatusHistory
expected_models.purpose: Immutable history of every canonical fulfillment state transition, separate from AuditEvent.

expected_models.name: FulfillmentCommandReceipt
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped idempotency receipt for mutable fulfillment commands.

expected_features: Create an explicit fulfillment batch only for a confirmed, non-cancelled Order.
Support multiple partial batches per Order without exceeding any confirmed OrderItem quantity.
Support delivery and pickup as canonical methods without shipping-provider integration.
Execute the approved fulfillment lifecycle through services with immutable status history.
Coordinate Order cancellation through a sanitized internal event: open batches are cancelled idempotently, completed history is preserved, and no batch may advance after the Order is cancelled.
Provide organization-scoped selectors, policies, server-rendered HTML, audit, and internal outbox events.
deferred_features: inventory reservation, stock movement, warehouse management, picking routes, and procurement
carrier quotation, label purchase or printing, tracking provider, freight pricing, and external logistics integration
failed-delivery, exchange, reverse logistics, return, and refund workflows
payment gating, payment links, financial states, Mercado Pago, Pagar.me, and Appmax
transactional messaging, public API, importers, webhooks, and external references
tax, accounting, fiscal documents, dashboards, deploy, Coolify, and legacy data import

methods.delivery_rule: Delivery copies the closed versioned shipping-address snapshot already frozen on the confirmed Order; an absent shipping address blocks creation.
methods.pickup_rule: Pickup requires an active OrganizationUnit from the same Organization and snapshots only its display name; unit-address management is deferred.

states.requirement: Proposed canonical state contract requiring human approval before implementation.
states.rule: These states belong only to Fulfillment and never rewrite Order.status; completed Order status, returns, financial states, and provider states remain absent.

quantity_rules: Use Decimal(12,3), matching the immutable confirmed OrderItem quantity; never float.
Every FulfillmentItem references an OrderItem from the same Order and Organization.
The sum of quantities in non-cancelled batches must not exceed the confirmed OrderItem quantity.
Allocation and cancellation lock the Order, relevant OrderItems, Fulfillments, and allocations in deterministic order.
Cancelling a batch releases its allocation; completed quantities remain historical.
Allocation is fulfillment planning only and does not create stock, reservation, cost, or inventory movement.
snapshots: Fulfillment item presentation uses the immutable name, variant, SKU, unit, and quantity from the confirmed OrderItem plus the allocated quantity.
Delivery destination is copied from the confirmed Order shipping snapshot into a closed schema_version 1 object; Customer changes never rewrite it.
Pickup snapshots the same-Organization OrganizationUnit name and identifier; it does not invent a unit address.
OPERATOR receives document, contact, and address data masked; only OWNER, ADMIN, and MANAGER may view unmasked personal data.
Addresses, contacts, documents, free-text reasons, and instructions never enter AuditEvent, OutboxEvent, logs, metrics, command receipts, or exception messages.
money_rules: Fulfillment persists no price, discount, surcharge, freight, fee, tax, interest, cost, or payment amount.
The approved BRL totals in Order remain the sole commercial source and are never recalculated or changed by Fulfillment.
Freight pricing and every financial effect remain deferred to separately approved contracts.
order_coordination: Fulfillment depends on the approved public contracts of Orders; Orders does not import Fulfillment and no cyclic app dependency is introduced.
Creation and every transition lock and revalidate the organization-scoped Order; draft or cancelled Orders are refused.
The existing sanitized order.cancelled outbox event is consumed idempotently inside the Vidalys Flow runtime to cancel non-completed batches with a system reason flag, not copied free text.
A completed batch is preserved as history if the commercial Order is later cancelled; returns and reverse logistics require a later approved contract.
Fulfillment completion is derived from its batches and never persists completed on Order.
idempotency: All mutable commands use FulfillmentCommandReceipt scoped by Organization, operation, and idempotency key.
The same key and canonical payload returns the previous result; a different payload is an explicit conflict.
Every mutation uses select_for_update and expected_version; retries never duplicate batches, allocations, transitions, history, audit, or outbox.
A batch sequence is increasing per Order and allocated while the Order is locked; its display form is PED-000001-F01.
The order.cancelled consumer deduplicates by source event ID and remains safe under retries and out-of-order delivery.
authorization: Organization comes from authenticated active Membership and is never accepted as a free request identifier.
Every service and selector receives Organization explicitly and resolves Order, Fulfillment, OrderItem, and OrganizationUnit within it.
OWNER, ADMIN, MANAGER, and OPERATOR may list, view masked operational data, create and edit draft batches, allocate quantities, and execute normal lifecycle transitions.
Only OWNER, ADMIN, and MANAGER may cancel a batch or view unmasked destination and contact data; cancellation requires a reason.
Cross-organization reads, writes, allocations, units, and event handling are refused and directly tested.

required: success and validation errors for delivery and pickup
authorization, PII masking, and cross-organization isolation
state transition success, method-specific refusal, and terminal states
concurrent creation, allocation, transition, and cancellation
Order cancellation event retry, out-of-order handling, and completed-history preservation
audit, outbox, logs, receipts, and exceptions sanitized of PII and free text
migration application and technical rollback from empty PostgreSQL
regression of Foundation, Customers, Products, and Orders

coverage.domain_expectation: Critical lifecycle, allocation, privacy, cancellation coordination, idempotency, and concurrency rules require direct behavioral tests.

documentation: architecture dependency graph and system flow
quantity, concurrency, idempotency, authorization, and privacy rules
explicit boundary with Orders, inventory, Payments, providers, Messaging, and Flowlog
updated roadmap through test, homologation, and deploy
acceptance_criteria: The plan and proposed lifecycle are explicitly approved before implementation.
Only allowed apps and features change; minimal Orders changes are adapters or sanitized event-contract additions covered by regressions.
No inventory, payment, provider, messaging, integration, fiscal, dashboard, infrastructure, or external effect is introduced.
Allocation never exceeds confirmed quantities, including under PostgreSQL concurrency.
Organization isolation, authorization, masking, sanitization, idempotency, and expected_version are enforced and tested.
Order cancellation coordination is idempotent and Fulfillment never mutates Order.status.
All quality gates and CI pass on the candidate HEAD.
Independent review has no unresolved blocker and QA/Security emits GO.
Human approval remains explicit before PR, merge, release, deploy, state approval, or the next phase.

handoff_format.base_sha_semantics: The exact origin/main SHA resolved before branch creation; this is actual_base_sha in checkpoint reports.

allowed_scope: Planning and, only after explicit plan approval, a new greenfield Fulfillment domain.
Minimal approved adapters to Orders, Organizations, Audit, and Platform contracts without cyclic dependencies.
New Fulfillment tests, migrations, server-rendered interfaces, documentation, audit, and internal outbox integration.
forbidden_scope: Starting Payments, Messaging, Integrations, Dashboard, inventory, infrastructure, homologation, cutover, or a later phase.
Calling carriers or providers, pricing freight, generating labels, reserving stock, charging, or sending messages.
Changing canonical Order states, money, commercial snapshots, or permission rules without separate explicit human authorization.
Reusing or consulting Flowlog code, data, migrations, runtime, IDs, secrets, services, providers, machines, or infrastructure.
Creating the implementation prompt before plan approval, implementing code during planning, merging, deploying, or configuring Coolify.
